collection.description: An elder sits outside at sunset and looks back over the whole of their life, without needing a verdict.

setup.name: The moment
setup.text: (name1) is sitting outside (his/her) hut as the sun goes down, the way (he/she) has on thousands of evenings. Tonight (he/she) finds (him/her)self looking back over the whole of it: the long, ordinary, surprising business of (his/her) life. Some of it went the way (he/she) hoped. A lot of it didn't. Some of the best parts were things (he/she) never planned at all. There are things (he/she) would do differently, and things (he/she) wouldn't change for anything, and a great many things (he/she) has simply forgotten. (He/She) tries to decide whether it has been a good life, and finds (he/she) can't quite say, and that (he/she) doesn't really need to. The sky goes orange, then pink, then a deep, soft blue. Somebody calls out that dinner is ready. (name1) gets up, slowly, and goes to eat.
